newsitem.title: FRANCE: Goldsmith's Europe of Nations rises from the ashes.
newsitem.headline: Goldsmith's Europe of Nations rises from the ashes.

text.p: The defunct anti-federalist Europe of Nations (EDN) group in the European Parliament, led by British billionaire Sir James Goldsmith, rose from the ashes on Monday.

The tiny 18-member EDN collapsed last November when one of its members defected to the large Christian Democrat European Peoples Party (EPP), leaving it one short of the minimum number of Euro-MPs needed to form a political party.

Its rebirth as the Group of Independents for the Europe of Nations was made possible by the decision of Ulster Unionist James Nicholson to defect the other way, leaving the pro-European EPP at the end of December 1996.
Arch Euro-sceptic Goldsmith also heads the Referendum Party in Britain, which he created with the sole purpose of forcing a referendum on Britain's role in the European Union.

The Ulster Unionist Party (UUP) said on December 23 its alliance with Anglo-French financier Goldsmith's EDN in the EU's directly elected assembly would not affect how it votes in the British parliament.

Now that he has lost his majority in the lower House of Commons, British Prime Minister John Major depends for survival on the support of the nine Ulster Unionist MPs, who represent Northern Ireland's pro-British Protestant majority.
The alliance is a warning to Major that the Ulster Unionists' votes cannot be taken for granted in the run-up to Britian's general election, which must be held by May 22.

In return for Nicholson's allegiance to Goldsmith's European faction, the Referendum Party has pledged to support the Ulster Unionists' campaign in Northern Ireland on the specific issue of a plebiscite on Britain's role in the EU.
The alliance has split the UUP, Northern Ireland's largest political party.
